articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts ruled out for Week 6 after blood clot found in his leg
articles.summary: The issue was discovered last week while the Eagles were in London.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot.

The team released a statement Thursday saying that Hurts asked the Eagles' training staff to treat his calf on Oct. 8 after being cleated during Philadelphia's game against the Los Angeles Rams days earlier. An ultrasound was performed on Oct. 10 after the team flew to London. The results showed a superficial blood clot, but doctors and medical staff concluded "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play."

The team says Hurts, who did not carry an injury designation before the game, played "without limitation" last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars and was able to practice fully Wednesday after receiving treatment earlier in the week.

A follow-up ultrasound was done Wednesday which "revealed movement in the small blood clot."

Hurts will miss Week 6 and it's unknown if he will be out beyond Sunday. The Eagles say they are determining the "appropriate course of treatment" and have been in communication with the NFL regarding the matter.

Tanner McKee, who has played six career NFL games since being drafted in 2023, will be the Eagles' starter.

articles.title: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Sues to Have Evidence in His Battery Case Permanently Sealed
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has filed a lawsuit seeking to have evidence in his battery case permanently sealed.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has filed a lawsuit seeking to have evidence in his battery case permanently sealed.

The lawsuit against the Hobart-Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department was filed Wednesday in Brown County Circuit Court.

Jacobs pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend. He was charged in late August, and the criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman's statement.

Jury Finds Tyreek Hill Liable for 2 Battery Counts (AP)

That video hasn't been released, and lawyers representing the woman filed a motion last month asking that the evidence be sealed.

Clarence Duchac, the lawyer representing Jacobs in this lawsuit, said in his complaint that Jacobs "joins and supports (the victim's) position that the identifying, private and sensitive records associated with the underlying incident should not be publicly released."

Shortly after Jacobs was charged, the NFL placed him on the commissioner's exempt list , which prevents the three-time Pro Bowler from playing or practicing but allows him to keep receiving a paycheck. NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said Thursday that the matter remains under review of the league's personal conduct policy and that there's no timeline on a decision.

In the complaint, Duchac says that public release of records identifying the victim or disclosing sensitive information about her "would force unwanted exposure upon her and risk revictimizing her through renewed public scrutiny."

The complaint says the police should be prohibited from publicly releasing "descriptions, images, audio recordings, video recordings, statements, communications, or other materials" whose disclosure might threaten the woman's "privacy, dignity, safety, emotional well-being, or ability to obtain closure."

The complaint also notes that public sports figures have recently been targeted for robberies and other related property crimes, and that releasing the video would reveal details of the garage's interior that might put Jacobs at risk.

"The public availability of (Jacobs') schedule or travel information increases the risk that persons could identify periods when (Jacobs) is away from home and use released information concerning the residence, garage, access points, security arrangements, or property to target the property," the complaint says. "Widespread public dissemination of those details would materially increase (Jacobs') vulnerability to theft, burglary, robbery, trespass, or other targeted criminal conduct."

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

Under an agreement Jacobs reached with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge against him can be dismissed in a year if he fulfills terms that include staying out of trouble, avoiding the victim in this case, submitting to supervision, completing counseling and paying restitution to the victim.

articles.title: Josh Allen signed a $330 million Bills contract with $250 million guaranteed in 2025 but chose a team-friendly deal to prioritize Super Bowl success over maximizing his market value
articles.summary: Josh Allen signed a six-year, $330 million extension with the Buffalo Bills on March 9, 2025, and $250 million of it counts as guaranteed, the most in NFL
articles.body: Josh Allen signed a six-year, $330 million extension with the Buffalo Bills on March 9, 2025, and $250 million of it counts as guaranteed, the most in NFL history. The numbers around the edges tell a quieter story. His $55 million average sits below Dak Prescott's $60 million, and his first-year cap hit actually dropped. Buffalo gained room to build a roster while the reigning MVP gave up some leverage. More than a year later, there is still no Super Bowl, so the trade deserves a fair look.Why Josh Allen's $330 million deal was built around the rosterJosh Allen had four years left on his old contract when this deal happened. He had no real need to sign. He could have waited, watched quarterback prices climb again, and asked for more. According to ESPN, the talks began at his end-of-season meeting with general manager Brandon Beane, and the extension followed about six weeks after the AFC title game loss to Kansas City.The structure shows the priority. The old deal had roughly $130 million left. The new one added two years and folded that money into a bigger package, yet the early cap numbers barely moved. His 2025 cap hit fell from about $44 million to $41.3 million. Through 2028, his numbers stay close to what the old contract already carried. The Bills had released Von Miller the same day and were near the cap limit, so that breathing room mattered more than any headline total.What the $250 million guarantee really meansThe figure is real, but it depends on how you count. Allen received $147 million guaranteed at signing. The rest consists of rolling guarantees that lock in over time, through March 2029. That is why Deshaun Watson's $230 million, fully guaranteed from day one, can still claim to be the cleaner record. Allen's camp counts everything, which is how $250 million becomes the headline.Neither view is wrong, and the split is useful. Spotrac lists $220 million due over the first four seasons. That is real protection. Buffalo cannot walk away cheaply early, and Allen knows it. So he traded top-of-market pace for security. A quarterback who wanted the loudest number would have pushed the average higher. Allen pushed the floor higher instead.Where Josh Allen gave groundStart with the average. Prescott's $60 million tops the league, and Allen's $55 million sits behind it. Patrick Mahomes still holds the largest total value, a ten-year, $450 million deal from 2020. Allen's contract is huge, but it is not the biggest by either measure.Then there are the smaller details. Allen can earn an extra $500,000 each year, but only if he plays 60 percent of the regular season snaps, 60 percent of the Super Bowl snaps, and wins the Super Bowl. For a man making this much, half a million is symbolic. It is also telling. The one bonus in the deal is tied to a championship.His willingness to turn salary into prorated bonuses has kept paying off for the team. In March 2026, Buffalo restructured the deal again and created $12 million in cap space, lowering his 2026 hit to $44.2 million. Allen said when the extension was signed that if the deal affected the cap, they should find a way around it. A year later, the contract is still doing that job.Has the bargain bought a Super Bowl yet?Not yet. The 2025 Bills went 12-5 and beat Jacksonville in the wild card round. Then they lost 33-30 in overtime to Denver in the divisional round. Allen also played through a late-season foot injury. Joe Brady, who built Allen's offense as coordinator, now runs the team as head coach.This is where honest analysis gets uncomfortable. Cap room is only worth what the team does with it. A discount that Buffalo turns into depth at edge rusher, linebacker, and receiver helps Allen win. A discount that sits unused is just a gift. Allen has also had a lot of postseason success, with 29 career playoff touchdown passes, so the quarterback is rarely the weak point when the Bills go out. The supporting cast is.Allen has said that becoming a father has changed his mindset heading into 2026. That is a personal note, not a contract term, but it fits. He is 30 now and has been paid like a franchise cornerstone since 2018's seventh overall pick. The remaining question is what he does with the room he helped create.The 2029 bill comes dueHere is the catch. The contract is cheap now because the cost has been pushed back. His scheduled cap hits run $61.4 million in 2026, $58.1 million in 2027, and $64.3 million in 2028. Then 2029 jumps to $86.1 million, about 21 percent of the cap by Spotrac's math. In 2030, it is $79.8 million.Most observers expect another restructure or extension well before that spike arrives. That is normal for quarterback deals, and nobody should treat $86 million as a real number. But it means the "team-friendly" label has an expiry date. Allen's flexibility is a loan, and Buffalo will have to repay it around the time he turns 33. articles.title: Josh Jacobs files civil suit to block release of his records from offseason arrest
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs is still on the commissioner's exempt list following an offseason arrest.
articles.body:
Content warning: The following article contains depictions of alleged battery.

Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is trying to prevent the release of records stemming from his offseason arrest. Jacobs filed a civil suit against the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department after it was approved to release certain records from the arrest with redactions.

The suit, which was filed by Jacobs on Wednesday, calls for a "permanent injunction, protective order, and order restricting access to records." Essentially, Jacobs wants to prevent any evidence from his arrest — including surveillance footage — from being released publicly. Shortly after Jacobs' arrest in May , it was reported surveillance video of Jacobs' alleged battery existed and corroborated the victim's claims of what transpired.

Ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list. He has not played in a single game this season due to that designation.

With Jacobs unable to play, the running back sought to resolve his legal situation quickly. In September, he pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property.

That paved the way for the NFL to make a ruling on a possible punishment for Jacobs. In previous instances, the NFL has typically waited until the legal process plays out before issuing a potential punishment against a player. At the time, however, the NFL said it was still gathering information on Jacobs' arrest.

A few weeks later, a judge denied the victim's request to permanently seal all evidence, including the surveillance video. Evidence was then turned over Hobart-Lawrence Police Department, which decided Tuesday that it would release certain records from the arrest.

In the civil suit, which has been obtained by multiple news outlets , Jacobs' attorneys argue any evidence released could result in the victim being identified, even with the proper redactions. They also argue that the surveillance footage would show the interior of Jacobs' garage, which could be viewed by burglars who target the homes of professional athletes.

If Jacobs is unable to get the evidence permanently sealed, it would open the door for the NFL to obtain the surveillance video of the incident that led to his arrest. In that footage, Jacobs allegedly grabbed the victim and threw her to the ground.

That footage could determine the length and severity of Jacobs' punishment from the league, making it a potentially significant piece in the NFL's ruling. Given the video's importance, the NFL will likely wait until Jacobs' civil suit is resolved before making a decision on the running back's future.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Takes Blame for Commanders' Clock Management vs. Giants, 'It Will Never Happen Again'
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels took responsibility for the clock management blunder that ended the Washington Commanders' 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants on Sunday.
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels took responsibility for the clock management blunder that ended the Washington Commanders' 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants on Sunday.

"It will never happen again," he told reporters Thursday. "I'm moving on to San Francisco. … Can't say [the criticism] is not warranted. … Can't stop no one from saying their opinion about my process."

The Commanders were in field-goal range in the final seconds of overtime and could have kicked it for the win. However, Daniels took a snap, appeared confused with the ball in his hands and was then tackled in bounds as the clock continued running.

Washington didn't have any timeouts and was unable to line up in time to spike it, so the game ended in a tie.

"As a competitor, you feel like you let everyone down," he said .

Daniels also expressed support for head coach Dan Quinn:

It was a fitting ending for an ugly overtime.

New York started the extra period with a missed field goal, which gave the Commanders a chance to win it with any points. However, the home team had to punt, giving the Giants the same chance.

It seemed like the visitors were going to win when they advanced to Washington's 24-yard line, but Cam Skattebo lost a fumble and gave the Commanders another chance to win it.

That's when Daniels directed the offense into scoring range before the mistake at the end of the game.

Things don't get much easier for the 1-3-1 Commanders, who now must go on the road to face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. Another loss would put them in quite a hole going into the bye week even with Daniels back and healthy after he missed multiple games with an elbow injury.

New York is in first place in the NFC East at 3-1-1, although Washington will have another opportunity at the division leaders in a rematch on Nov. 12.

Daniels' comments suggest he will be much better prepared to handle end-of-game situations than he was in the first matchup.

articles.title: Raiders' Ashton Jeanty Gives Injury Update Ahead of Bills Game, Says He's 'Ready to Go'
articles.summary: After dealing with injuries to start the season, Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty provided a positive update on Thursday.
articles.body:
After dealing with injuries to start the season, Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty provided a positive update on Thursday.

The second-year player says he's "ready to go" for this week's matchup against the Buffalo Bills, adding that this is the best he's felt all season and he's starting overcome the mental battle.

"I think anytime you sustain any type of injury, that's more of a battle you face," Jeanty said.

Jeanty has yet to miss time this season, but it's clear that he hasn't been 100 percent. He was limited to just 10 carries against the New England Patriots last week, recording 27 yards, though he added three receptions for 50 yards.

ESPN's Dan Graziano noted on Wednesday that the Raiders will likely give Jeanty a week to recover from his early ailments and gear up for the second half of the season.

"Jeanty has been bothered by an ankle injury since the preseason and is now dealing with a foot injury as well," Graizano wrote. "He was questionable to play Sunday and only got cleared after a nine-minute pregame workout and discussion with team trainers and coaches. But keep an eye on this situation. The Raiders have internally discussed giving Jeanty a week off to heal at some point."

It remains to be seen whether Las Vegas still plans to let Jeanty rest soon, but his comments on Thursday indicate that he feels at least close to 100 percent. Graziano also noted that Jeanty doesn't want to miss any time and has pushed through his injuries so far.

The Raiders don't have their bye week until Week 13, so it's not a bad idea to give Jeanty a break before that if he's still managing injuries.

Jeanty had 975 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie and has recorded 291 rushing yards so far this year, adding 215 yards and two touchdowns through the air.

While Jeanty hasn't gotten going the way he and Las Vegas hoped, the Raiders are still off to a surprising 3-2 start. They've dropped their last two games, though, and have a tough matchup on deck against Josh Allen and the Bills.

articles.title: Final voter list in UP to be published on Jan 4, 2027
articles.summary: ECI sets UP special electoral roll revision: polling station reorganisation by Nov 2, 2026; draft rolls Nov 12; final voter list published Jan 4, 2027.
articles.body: Lucknow: Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced the schedule for the special summary revision of electoral rolls across all Assembly constituencies in the state, with the final electoral rolls scheduled for publication on Jan 4, 2027.Chief electoral officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said on Thursday that the revision would be conducted with Jan 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for determining voter eligibility.According to the schedule, the rationalisation and reorganisation of polling stations will be completed by Nov 2, 2026, while the draft electoral rolls will be published on Nov 12.Voters will have one month, from Nov 12 to Dec 11, to submit claims and objections regarding the inclusion, deletion or correction of names in the electoral rolls.The electoral authorities will examine and dispose of all claims and objections by Dec 28, following which the final electoral rolls will be published on Jan 4, 2027.Rinwa said meetings with recognised political parties would be organised at both the state and district levels to explain Election Commission’s guidelines and revision procedures.District election officers have been instructed to make the necessary arrangements and ensure compliance with the prescribed schedule.The exercise aims to update electoral rolls ahead of the assembly elections, ensuring that all eligible voters are included and necessary corrections are made before the final publication.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: ESPN is about to make a tragic mistake, college football team hangs with cheerleaders & MLB's Abby Labar!
articles.summary: Troy Aikman didn't deny the reported argument with Joe Buck, saying he'll be a free agent after this season as ESPN faces a massive decision.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Over the hump and safely into a big Thursday — which, during the fall, is basically the start of the weekend. Congrats, you made it! Football tonight. Playoff baseball this afternoon AND tonight. More football tomorrow. And the next day. And the day after that! Who has it better than us right now? We're halfway through October, which is a bummer. That just means we need to appreciate this time even more. And we will. Let's roll. Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where ESPN is about to make one of the dumbest decisions it has made in years, which is saying something given its recent history. BREAKING UP TROY AIKMAN AND JOE BUCK WOULD BE A BIG MISTAKE FOR ESPN | BOBBY BURACK What else? I've got Western Kentucky players partying with Sam Houston State cheerleaders after destroying the Bearkats last night, Dodgers fans are getting DRAGGED through the mud today, and MLB Network's Abby Labar checks in on this third Thursday of October. OK, grab you a headset and head on up to the ESPN booth because you could be next in line on Monday nights, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap! ESPN isn't gonna do this, are they? I hate to start with a competitor today, but ESPN has left me no choice. Obviously, the big story in the sports media world today is the ongoing riff between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. It started to percolate a few days ago when a report said the two had an argument before Monday night's game in LA, and it all stems from the fact the Buck recently signed a contract extension with ESPN. Troy — Joe's longtime partner in the booth — has not. Some threw cold water on the report, which came from Front Office Sports. Some. Not Troy. Take a listen: SUPER BOWL LXI GETS PAT MCAFEE TREATMENT AS ESPN ADDS ALTERNATE BROADCAST This would be a stunning, and stupid, move to make "There’s probably a time and a place for all that. I don’t know if now is the time," Aikman said when asked about it this morning. "I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened. I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. "I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be." Lordy. Couple things ... There's also this little video that's making the rounds in the wake of the reported argument. It was taken by a fan before Monday's game in LA, and shows Buck and his wife appearing to have some sort of ... disagreement? ... on the field during warm-ups: Could be nothing, but ... it could also be something. My take? I'd be stunned if ESPN let Aikman go. Stunned. These two were a package deal when they joined ESPN a few years ago, and, by all accounts (ratings!), it's been one of the very few successes at the company in the last decade. As for potential landing spots for Aikman should ESPN not pony up ... Bottom line? ESPN would be INSANE to do this. But, as we've learned through the years, ESPN is a generally insane company. The good news? For you McAfee haters out there, you don't have to worry about him joining the booth any time soon: Western Kentucky had a big night, Dodgers fans did NOT & reader mail! Could you imagine the absolute outrage if ESPN put Pat McAfee in the MNF booth? The internet would burn. Part of me just wants to see it happen for the meltdown. Sadly, it appears to be a silly rumor, which almost NEVER happens on the internet! OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big night of FOOTBALL! First up? I've spent all day kicking myself for putting actual US currency on the Sam Houston Bearkats last night. They got smoked by Western Kentucky, and looked lifeless the entire game. The Hilltoppers won, 16-3 (miserable game to watch), and then proceeded to rub salt in the wound when the final buzzer rang: Incredible. What a move by these Western Kentucky players. Beating the brakes off a team on its home turf is one thing, but to then put the moves on its cheerleaders when it's all said and done is next-level psychological warfare. That's tough to come back from as a program ... CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE And so is this, for you Dodgers fans: Lordy. Brutal — and I mean brutal — showing for the LA faithful last night. No sugar-coating that. The internet has ganged up on the Rays throughout these playoffs for the empty seats at The Trop, so we have to be fair and hammer the Dodgers here. articles.title: “Take The Attention And Run With It”: Marcellus Wiley’s Advice To WNBA About Elle Duncan’s Stance On “Toxic” Casual Fans
articles.summary: The WNBA has become part of the national discourse this season, mainly for political and not athletic reasons. But that isn’t necessarily a bad thing, says f...
articles.body:
The WNBA has become part of the national discourse this season, mainly for political and not athletic reasons. But that isn't necessarily a bad thing, says former NFL player Marcellus Wiley. It can actually be the start of a better relationship between the public and the league, and casual fans are key to this.

Speaking on a video posted to his X account this Wednesday, Wiley railed against the culture of some around the WNBA who believe that casual fans aren't necessary for the sport and league to grow.

In his critique of this mindset, Wiley said:

"What's wrong with a casual? A casual buys a jersey, a wristband; a casual turns on the TV, gives you a little rating bump; a casual has a conversation that spreads to somebody who is a real fan. But what is this real fan culture?… What does it matter? Take the attention and run with it," said Marcellus Wiley.

He also made a comparison to the NFL, noting that as a kid he was only able to attend one of the league's games. He said that didn't mean he didn't love the league; it just showed how few opportunities there were for him to attend. In the same vein, casual fans, he argues, could help the WNBA grow nationally.

WNBA celebrates record viewership numbers in 2026 season

This Wednesday, the WNBA released a statement by Commissioner Cathy Engelbert celebrating what they called a record-breaking season for viewership and fan engagement.

"The league's 30th season has been one to remember, with extraordinary fan engagement, record viewership, packed arenas and spectacular basketball," said WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert. "For three decades, generations of players, teams, fans and so many others have dedicated themselves to building this league and making a season like this possible. There is tremendous pride in what we've accomplished together and even greater excitement for all that lies ahead."

According to their press release, the league achieved a record of 90 million viewers this season, with 51 broadcasts attracting at least 1 million viewers. They also celebrated 3.8 million fans attending their games in person.

articles.title: Packers Face ‘Hair on Fire’ Cowboys Duo in Emotional Reunion
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers will see a couple of players on the opposing sideline they know well.Former Packers defensive standouts Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary are...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers will see a couple of players on the opposing sideline they know well.

Former Packers defensive standouts Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary are returning to Lambeau Field as members of the Dallas Cowboys, setting up an intriguing reunion for Week 6 on Sunday night.

Both players spent notable portions of their careers in Green Bay, with Clark becoming a three-time Pro Bowler and Gary emerging as one of the team's most recognizable pass rushers.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur expects the duo to have a bundle of motivation when they line up against their former teammates.

"I expect them to be playing with their hair on fire," LaFleur said, per Ryan Wood of USA TODAY .

Clark, Gary Prepare for Emotional Packers Reunion

Clark's history with the Packers stretches back to 2016, when Green Bay selected him in the first round of the NFL draft out of UCLA.

The defensive tackle developed into a cornerstone of the Packers' defensive front, earning three Pro Bowl selections during his nine seasons with the organization.

His tenure ended in August 2025, when Green Bay sent Clark to Dallas as part of the blockbuster trade that brought Micah Parsons to the Packers.

Gary followed a different way out of town.

Green Bay traded the former Michigan standout to Dallas in March 2026 for a fourth-round selection in the 2027 NFL draft, ending his seven-year run with the franchise.

The two defenders spent six seasons together in Green Bay and now have an opportunity to face their former team on the same night.

Clark acknowledged the emotional significance of his return during an Oct. 14 interview .

"I was there nine years. That's one of my homes," Clark said. "I got drafted there at 20 years old, became a man there."

Gary expressed similar appreciation for the organization and its supporters, though he emphasized that the Cowboys' priorities are more important than the reunion.

"Being able to go back to a fanbase that started with me, watched me grow, watched me excel, do good things there, it's going to be good," Gary said.

Packers Face Former Teammates Amid Cowboys' Defensive Struggles

LaFleur's warning also lands at a crossroads in Gary's career.

The 28-year-old has struggled to institute himself as a consistent difference-maker in Dallas, recording just one sack through his first five games of the 2026 season.

His performance has drawn criticism, particularly after the Cowboys' loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5.

ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky recently questioned the effort of Gary, Clark and fellow Dallas defensive lineman Quinnen Williams .

"Their effort isn't good enough," Orlovsky said .

Gary has a shot to deliver a statement against the organization that traded him away, and Clark can remind Green Bay why he was such an vital piece of its defense for nearly a decade.

The Cowboys are also dealing with defensive concerns, including problems stopping opposing offenses often.

Clark acknowledged that Dallas must improve up front and specifically pointed toward Green Bay's struggling rushing attack.

"They haven't been running the ball well this year," Clark said in his Wednesday media availability .

The matchup may serve multiple moments for LaFleur to capitalize on Dallas' defensive shortcomings, even though the Packers will have to account for two players who are intimately familiar with the organization.

And with the reunion taking place under the lights at Lambeau Field, the emotions may run high. And LaFleur certainly expects Clark and Gary to bring their best effort.

articles.title: Agency Representing Brock Purdy Announces Odell Beckham Jr. as Its New Client After Giants Exit
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. ’s latest move extends beyond the football field.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. 's latest move extends beyond the football field. After his reunion with the New York Giants ended with his release, the veteran wide receiver has signed with Range Sports for off-field representation, joining an agency that also represents San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy.

"We are thrilled to announce Odell Beckham Jr. is now a Range Sports client," Range Sports' LinkedIn post read on Thursday .

Range Sports, part of Range Media Partners, will handle Beckham's marketing and brand partnerships, broadcasting, on-air work, scripted film and television opportunities, and other business ventures . Klutch Sports will continue to represent him for his on-field career, keeping the two sides of his professional life separate.

The agreement also brings Beckham's production company, 2463 Entertainment, into a partnership with Range Sports and Range Studios. The companies plan to develop, package, produce, and sell projects across film, television, documentaries, and digital content.

One project already in the works is OBJ: I Am Who I Am , a documentary about Beckham's life and career that the companies plan to take to market soon.

Range announced the deal by pointing to Beckham's reach across sports, fashion, entertainment and business. The agency described him as a player whose profile extends well beyond his NFL career.

"Odell is one of the most recognizable and influential athletes of his generation," Range Sports executives Jake Dexter and Lowell Taub said in a joint statement, adding that the partnership offers an opportunity to turn Beckham's influence across sports, culture, fashion and entertainment into lasting content and intellectual property.

Dexter, Range's vice president of sports content, will lead the work involving Beckham and 2463 Entertainment. Taub, the agency's chief revenue officer, will oversee endorsements and media opportunities.

The agency's existing NFL connection adds another notable name to the announcement. Purdy, who leads the 49ers' offense, is represented by Range Sports, with Kyle Strongin serving as his primary NFL agent.

Beckham set up 2463 Entertainment in 2024. He wants to develop films, TV shows, documentaries and digital content through the company. Now, Range will help him take those projects from development to potential buyers while he continues his NFL career.

The move comes as Beckham tries to get his playing career back on track. He returned to the Giants this season but appeared in just three games, playing 19 snaps without recording a catch. New York released him on September 29, ending a reunion with the franchise that selected him 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft.

The Minnesota Vikings subsequently signed Beckham to their practice squad, giving the 33-year-old another chance to contribute on the field. He previously played for the Cleveland Browns, Los Angeles Rams, Baltimore Ravens, and Miami Dolphins. His NFL career includes 575 receptions for 7,987 yards and 59 touchdowns.

While his role in Minnesota remains a separate matter, the Range agreement gives Beckham a broader team to help manage his business interests. With the documentary and other projects in development, his next career moves could extend well beyond Sundays.

articles.title: How Browns are dealing with injuries ahead of Ravens game
articles.summary: The Browns continue to deal with multiple major injuries, while also monitoring the Ravens' quarterback situation ahead of their game.
articles.body:
BEREA ― The storyline of the week for the Browns as they prepare for the Baltimore Ravens in a critical AFC North home game has been injuries.

There's the rather lengthy list of injuries which the Browns are dealing with, including nine starters who either didn't practice or were limited Oct. 15. Then there's the rather significant injury question hanging over the Ravens most important player, as quarterback Lamar Jackson was not seen on the practice field again by Baltimore reporters.

The two questions bring out two different answers from the Browns. The gist of both, though, centers around the idea of contolling what they can control.

Cleveland Browns vs New York Jets: Best photos from Week 5 NFL game

"That's the tale of football," Browns defensive end Jared Verse said Oct. 15. "No matter what happens, you always got to be ready for the next person up. Whether you're in third string, whether you're on scout, whether you're just at home waiting to get a call from somebody to come in and play, you got to have your mindset ready."

The side of the football where the injuries ― and the Ravens' quarterback situation ― are having the biggest impact are on the defensive side of the ball. The only offensive starter who didn't practice was running back Quinshon Judkins, who missed his second day of practice due to an ankle injury, while right tackle Tytus Howard (knee), tight end Carsen Ryan (calf) and running back Dylan Sampson returned.

Another piece of good news for the offense: Wide receiver KC Concepcion (concussion) practiced for the second day in the row. His status remains up in the air, although special teams coordinator Byron Storer spoke specifically to his potential to handle punt return dutitres.

"Yeah, we just see how the week goes and see how he's feeling and then make the necessary decisions according to how he's feeling and if he's available," Storer said. "But as of right now, we're preparing as if we don't have him."

The Browns had five key defensive players sidelined for the second practice in a row, including arguably two of their three best players: Defensive tackle Mason Graham (knee, ankle) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle). Graham is one of three defensive tackles who didn't practice, along with Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) and Kalia Davis (quad), who is a week into his 21-day return to practice from injured reserve, while the fifth was defensive end Derek Barnett (ankle).

Cleveland did play the New York Jets in Week 5 without Graham and Hall, with Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington, plus practice-squad call-ups Sam Kamara and Chris Williams, stepping in. The absence of Barnett would put additional pressure on Verse, Isaiah McGuire and Sam Williams at end, while Easton Mascarenas-Arnold would be first up if Schwesinger can't go.

"We have the greatest group of guys who are full of spirit," Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg said. "I mean, you see the way we practice today and yesterday. There's tons of spirit. Our competitive nature is awesome. And we have a bunch of guys who play to our style. They play for each other. They play hard as hell. We're constantly trying to find different ways to create edges, and that's the mind part. And then in the end, it's our fist. And you see that every day from our group of guys, no matter who's out there. And that's the coolest part about being out there with them and being a part of it."

That defense, whoever is available to play, is looking more and more likely that they'll be facing a backup quarterback when the Ravens come to town. Jackson was absent for the second practice of the week for the Ravens, not a great sign for his availability since he last played in the first half of their Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4.

Tyler "Snoop" Huntley would get his second start of the season if Jackson can't ultimately go. He was 24-of-32 for 201 yards and two touchdowns plus a 111.6 passer rating in the Ravens' overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5.

"Yes, there are challenges every week, whether it's a new quarterback or you have different wideouts, different tight ends," Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle told Baltimore reporters Oct 15. "You lose guys throughout the year. I've said it to the group, but it's all about just fixing this week's problems. So, you figure out what the problems are this week, how do we minimize those things, how do we take advantage of giving our guys that are up and that are playing, the best chance to go win the game and to be able to execute at a high level?"

In Jackson, the Ravens have one of the greatest dual-threat quarterbacks in NFL history. The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player remains the NFL's leader in passer rating (119.6) and average yards per pass attempt (10.1) despite only playing in three-and-a-half games.

Jackson has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while completing 70.8% of his passes He's averaging 7.6 yards on 19 rushing attempts with a touchdown, and is the NFL's all-time career and single-season rushing leader among quarterbacks.

Whoever is at quarterback could be monitoring some questions at wide receiver. Zay Flowers was added to the injury list as limited on Oct. 15 with a toe issue, while Rashod Bateman did not practice a day after being limited due to shoulder and knee issues.

"I mean, we're playing the Ravens," Rutenberg said. "Lamar, Snoop, both elite quarterbacks. I mean, Lamar's all… everything he's done speaks for itself. And you see every time Snoop's in there, they win a lot of games. He's highly productive. And then it's the quarterback. It's the great running backs of Derrick Henry and Justice Hill. The tight ends, Mark Andrews has been doing it a long time. They've brought new guys in. They're doing it at a high level. They got really good receivers, the O-line. We've got to prepare for the Ravens."

articles.title: Former Packers Star Makes Stunning Jared Goff Declaration
articles.summary: Former Packers WR Greg Jennings makes a bold declaration about Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff following his historic start to 2026.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions have heard plenty of criticism about quarterback Jared Goff over the years, but one former Green Bay Packers star has apparently seen enough. And his latest assessment should have Lions fans smiling.

Former Packers wide receiver Greg Jennings believes Goff deserves to be considered the best quarterback in the NFL right now. That is quite a statement, especially considering Detroit is preparing to host Jennings' former team on October 25.

And Jennings has the numbers to back up his argument.

Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Greg Jennings Makes Bold Jared Goff Declaration

During a recent appearance on First Things First , Jennings made his case for Goff while discussing the NFL's top quarterbacks.

"He should be atop the mountain," Jennings said , pointing to Goff's historic start to the season.

The former Packers receiver emphasized that Goff's success often gets overlooked because he doesn't play the same flashy style as quarterbacks such as Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. While those players make headlines with their athleticism, Goff continues producing impressive numbers from the pocket.

Jennings also explained that Jahmyr Gibbs' success is connected to Goff's ability to put teammates in favorable situations. As his comments highlighted , Detroit's quarterback deserves more recognition for making the players around him better.

Jared Goff's Numbers Are Getting Hard to Ignore

Through five games, Goff has thrown for 1,485 yards, 12 touchdowns, and zero interceptions . Those are remarkable numbers for a quarterback leading an offense that also features one of the league's most productive rushing attacks.

In fact, Detroit has become the first team in NFL history to feature a quarterback with at least 1,400 passing yards and 12 passing touchdowns alongside a running back with at least 500 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through five games.

Goff's individual performance has already generated plenty of discussion. We recently highlighted how Goff owns the NFL's highest passing grade among qualifying quarterbacks , providing another argument for his place among the league's elite.

And the respect isn't limited to national television personalities. Following Detroit's 45-21 victory over Arizona, Goff credited Sam LaPorta for helping transform the Lions' offense , demonstrating the leadership and willingness to recognize teammates that have become hallmarks of his time in Detroit.

The Packers Are About to Get a Close-Up Look

Perhaps the most interesting part of Jennings' comments is the timing. Detroit will welcome Green Bay to Ford Field following its bye week, giving Goff an opportunity to reinforce the former Packers receiver's argument against a division rival.

Of course, five outstanding games don't automatically make someone the NFL's best quarterback. Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, and several others have impressive résumés of their own.

But Goff's 2026 performance deserves serious consideration, regardless of how anyone ranks the league's quarterbacks. If he continues protecting the football while producing touchdowns at this rate, the MVP conversation is only going to get louder.

And hearing a former Packers star lead that conversation?

That makes it even sweeter for Lions fans.

articles.title: Chargers' Khalil Mack linked to shocking trade with division rival
articles.summary: A trade proposal sees the Chargers sending edge rusher Khalil Mack to one of their biggest rivals.
articles.body:
The Chargers are expected to be one of the biggest sellers ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

Los Angeles was expected to possibly make a trade or two to add to their roster. However, a month into the season, they still haven't won a game, and at 0-5, they are on the verge of a fire sale.

It's all speculation for now, but it could become reality if they keep going down this road as the deadline approaches. One name at the top of the trade board is Khalil Mack.

The Chargers are expected to get a ton of calls on Mack in the coming weeks; however, this wild trade proposal would send the veteran edge rusher to one of their biggest rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs.

Bleacher Report's Alex Kay believes adding Mack is one move the Chiefs need to put them over the top.

Kansas City Chiefs receive: EDGE Khalil Mack

Los Angeles Chargers receive: 2027 fifth-round draft pick

"While Mack is one of the more decorated defenders of the modern era, he's yet to win a ring during his 13-year NFL career. Joining forces with the Chiefs would give him a chance to do so, as his presence shores up Kansas City's most glaring weakness and gives the club a far better chance of raising another banner."

While there's a good chance Mack gets traded in the coming weeks, the likelihood that the Chargers hand him over to the Chiefs is extremely low.

The Chiefs and Chargers are on two different paths this season. Kansas City is 4-0 and is right in the thick of the Super Bowl mix.

As for the Chargers, they were supposed to be on the same path as the Chiefs; however, their season has gone sideways.

The Chargers are 0-5, and it's unclear when they'll get their first win, as they are in the middle of their toughest stretch of the season.

Mack is desperate to make a deep playoff run and capture a Super Bowl title in his illustrious career. He won't do that with the Chargers, and the Chiefs give him a real shot.

articles.title: Burrow: Bengals ‘got to be better’ after Week 5 win as bye begins
articles.summary: CINCINNATI (AP) — In the aftermath of the Cincinnati Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Miami Dolphins, quarterback Joe Burrow was asked to evaluate the team throu...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — In the aftermath of the Cincinnati Bengals' Week 5 win over the Miami Dolphins, quarterback Joe Burrow was asked to evaluate the team through five games this season.

The Bengals enter the bye with a 3-2 record, and their next game will be an AFC North matchup as Cincinnati faces the Baltimore Ravens. The way that the Bengals entered the bye and the specifics of the game against the Dolphins showed what the Bengals need to improve.

"A lot of frustrating things on our end," Taylor said about the 31-24 win. "We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the 4-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown, gave them four points, and gave up over 200 yards rushing. Plenty to clean up."

The most important element of this bye week looks like a chance to get healthy. Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Bryan Cook have missed time over the past two weeks with various injuries, and the Bengals' depth at receiver and safety has been severely tested.

Also, the bye week comes after a taxing game in a record-setting October heat last Sunday in Miami.

"The bye hits us at a great time," Taylor said. "I know these guys are worn out. We've had some down-to-the-wire games the last three weeks. I know how hot this one was (in Miami). The bye week comes at a great time for us to be 3 -2. These guys will regroup. We know who we are. Today, there's a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks."

The biggest bright spot of the first five weeks of the season is that the Bengals learned the type of unit that it can have on defense. The front office heavily invested in the defense during the offseason, and the investments are paying off as Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe, Cashius Howell, Jonathan Allen and Cook hit the ground running.

"We're bringing life to each other," Mafe said. "We don't point fingers on this defense. If a guy makes a mistake, we've got you. We'll back you up. When you have that mentality, it's easy to play the game how you want to."

With Lawrence in the mix, the Bengals have gone from a team that had the lowest run stuff rate in the NFL in 2025 to the team with the highest run stuff rate in the NFL in 2026 through Week 5. Lawrence has also made a significant impact as a pass rusher with impact, drive-changing plays.

"He just loves it. It's contributed a lot to the personality of our defense," Taylor said. "That's what you really see from our guys. Not only are they talented and confident. They're playing with really good chemistry. They've got a really big personality as a whole. He's obviously a big part of that."

Mafe has become the Bengals' best true pass rusher. His consistent ability to win off the edge has sped up quarterbacks, produced turnovers and generated sacks for himself and his teammates.

"Right now, it's a mindset to go out there and show who I can be as a player," Mafe said. "With the coaches trusting me to be that player, it's up to me to uphold that in my end of the bargain."

The defense will need to keep making progress as the Bengals flip the page to the second half of the season. Expectations are high for a team that hasn't made the postseason since the 2022 season, and the Bengals' upcoming game in Baltimore sets up as a pivot point for the rest of the season.
